claim: WSTS statistics include estimates made by WSTS for semiconductor companies that do not participate in the survey, so the published world total is not purely member-reported data.
evidence: "The statistics presented in this report have been compiled on the basis of confidential data submitted by companies participating in the survey; estimates provided by WSTS, Inc. are included for nonparticipating companies worldwide." (Green Book 2018, p. 2, Program Overview)

claim: WSTS states that it adds estimates for non-participants wherever its membership covers less than 100% of a market segment, because it aims to represent the entire semiconductor market.
evidence: "As WSTS attempts to represent the entire semiconductor market in its reports, estimates are added for non-participants in cases where the WSTS membership covers less than 100% of the respective market segment." (WSTS, Basic Principles of Data Collection and Report Generation)

claim: When a participating WSTS member fails to submit data for a month, the data collection agents impute its input using that company's previously reported market share.
evidence: "To adjust for non-receipt of any participant's data, Moss Adams LLP, topserve.ch GmbH and Grant Thornton Taiyo (GTT) will use that company's previously reported market share to compute its input data for the current month." (Green Book 2018, p. 2)

claim: WSTS statistics cover non-captive semiconductor manufacturers only; chips made by a company solely for its own use are outside the stated reporting population.
evidence: "The report reflects worldwide statistics for all non-captive semiconductor manufacturers worldwide." (Green Book 2018, p. 2)
notes: How WSTS treats in-house chips designed by system companies (e.g. hyperscaler ASICs made by foundries) is not stated; see m_custom unknown.

claim: WSTS reports monthly net billings (shipments) from semiconductor manufacturers to end customers, authorised distributors, and divisions or subsidiaries that make end products.
evidence: "Reported data include all monthly net billings (shipments) between semiconductor manufacturers and their end customers, authorized distributors and divisions or subsidiaries that manufacture end products." (Green Book 2018, p. 2)

claim: Distributor resale is not counted a second time in the WSTS market: a chip sold through a distributor enters once, at the manufacturer's billing price to the distributor, so the WSTS total excludes distributor margins.
evidence: Our reading of the WSTS reporting definition (see m_billings).
notes: Based on @m_billings.

claim: WSTS assigns every billing to a region by the customer's shipment (ship-to) location, not by the seller's headquarters or where the chip was made.
evidence: "All billings are reported according to customer shipment location." (p. 2); Geographic Billing: "Dollar value of net billings into each region by ship-to location between non-captive semconductor manufacturers and their end customers, authorized distributors and divisions or subsidiaries that manufacture end products." (Green Book 2018, p. 3, Definitions)
notes: Resolves the unknown recorded in CLM-0080 (basis of regional attribution), for the 2019 edition of the definitions.

claim: WSTS values billings at actual sales prices, and internal transfers (e.g. to a manufacturer's own end-product divisions) at comparable market prices.
evidence: "Actual sales prices (or comparable market prices for internal transfers) are used to value all billings." (Green Book 2018, p. 2)
notes: Answers the subquestion whether publishers count chips at transfer value inside IDMs: WSTS uses comparable market price for internal transfers to end-product divisions.

claim: WSTS billings include non-recurring engineering (NRE) charges.
evidence: Bill: "Shipments made and billed by ship-to location, including NRE." (Green Book 2018, p. 3, Definitions)

claim: WSTS monthly statistics (2018 Green Book) were compiled by three data collection agents: Moss Adams LLP (Campbell), topserve.ch GmbH (Winterthur) and Grant Thornton Taiyo (Tokyo), which tabulated member data without audit.
evidence: "Compiled by Moss Adams LLP in Campbell, topserve.ch GmbH in Winterthur and Grant ThorntonTaiyo in Tokyo" (p. 1); "Because their work was limited to tabulating information furnished without audit, they can assume no responsibility for the accuracy of the underlying amounts." (p. 2)

claim: The names of companies participating in the WSTS survey and the public sources used for its non-participant estimates are disclosed only to participants, via the WSTS Administrator, not publicly.
evidence: "All participant inquiries with respect to the program, including the name of companies participating in the survey and the public sources used in compiling estimates, should be directed to the WSTS Administrator." (Green Book 2018, p. 2)
notes: Our reading of 'participant inquiries': the member list is not in any public WSTS page we opened.

claim: Public inquiries about WSTS data are handled by SIA for the Americas, Taiwan and China, by ESIA in Europe, by the WSTS Japan Council in Japan and by KSIA for the rest of Asia Pacific.
evidence: "All public inquiries concerning WSTS should be addressed to SIA in the Americas, Taiwan and China, to ESIA in Europe, to WSTS Japan Council in Japan and to KSIA in Asia Pacific (except for Taiwan and China)." (Green Book 2018, p. 2)

claim: WSTS publishes a consensus market forecast twice a year covering four years, produced from member companies' submitted outlooks and adjusted at a members' 'forecast meeting'.

claim: WSTS member companies enter monthly unit and revenue data online; regional data collection agents check and anonymise them and a worldwide agent aggregates the totals, with data published within about five weeks of month end.
evidence: "Individual semiconductor member companies enter unit sales and revenue data into a simple online form monthly. Data-collection agents (DCA) in the regions compile information from the companies." ... "Our worldwide DCA receives the regional data, further checks the information for consistency, aggregates totals" (slide 8); "published within five weeks of the closing of the month" (slide 2)

claim: WSTS added new wide-bandgap (SiC and GaN) product categories for power transistors and rectifiers in 2023/2024.
evidence: "WSTS introduced in 2023/2024 new wide bandgap product categories (SiC / GaN) for power transistors & rectifiers." (WSTS subscription presentation Oct 2024, slide 5)

claim: Companies acting as foundries cannot join WSTS as regular members and may instead take a 'foundry membership' subscription.
evidence: "Semiconductor Manufacturers who cannot join WSTS as Member for whatever reason (e.g. acting as a foundry) may enter a subscription with a foundry membership with WSTS." (WSTS Subscription - Foundry membership page)

claim: Because WSTS records billings of non-captive chip vendors at the point of sale to customers, and foundries are not reporting members, foundry wafer revenue is not a separate layer of the WSTS total; the value of foundry-made chips enters once, through the fabless or IDM vendor's own sale price.
evidence: Reasoning from m_billings, m_noncaptive and m_foundry; consistent with CLM-0009.
notes: Inference from @m_billings, @m_foundry, CLM-0002, CLM-0009. No WSTS text explicitly states the foundry treatment.

claim: The free WSTS Historical Billings Report gives monthly billings and three-month moving averages by four regions (Americas, Europe, Japan, Asia Pacific) from 1986, drawn from the WSTS Blue Book; the July 2026 edition had data to July 2026.
evidence: "Four decades of WSTS statistics from the WSTS Blue Book are now available for free download - with latest data from July 2026." ... claim: The free WSTS historical dataset contains regional totals only; annual product-category splits (discretes, optoelectronics, sensors, analog, micro, logic, memory) back to 1986 are not in it and are only public for recent years via forecast releases.
evidence: XLSX shared strings contain only region labels ("Worldwide", "Americas", "Europe", "Japan", "Asia Pacific"), month/quarter labels and "Total Year"; no product categories appear in either sheet.

claim: The free WSTS historical dataset does not split out China; China is included in 'Asia Pacific', although WSTS monthly subscriber statistics report China as a separate region.
evidence: XLSX regions are only "Americas", "Europe", "Japan", "Asia Pacific" and "Worldwide" ("sum of regions" per WSTS definitions); see CLM-0004 for the five-region subscriber data.
